title: 2.5 Adaptation and Mitigation Strategies to Climate Change
description: UNFCCC response strategies, adaptation types, Ethiopian practices and mitigation measures. Hard level.

questions.question: Why must mitigation and adaptation be pursued together?
options: They address different parts of the problem: causes and impacts
Local variations can mislead; the global mean reveals the trend
They extend beyond rising temperatures to ecosystems and storms
They store carbon and support economic and ecological functions
questions.correctAnswer: They address different parts of the problem: causes and impacts

questions.question: How does irrigation illustrate adaptation?
options: It adjusts farming practice to cope with changed water availability
They deliver electricity at virtually zero greenhouse gas emissions
It cycles material between the crust, mantle, oceans and atmosphere
Growing forests absorb and store carbon dioxide from the atmosphere
questions.correctAnswer: It adjusts farming practice to cope with changed water availability

questions.question: Why is natural-system adaptation described as reactive?
options: Species predict future climate precisely
It extends beneath part of the Atlantic Ocean
Natural systems follow government plans
Species respond after conditions have changed
questions.correctAnswer: Species respond after conditions have changed

questions.question: What does enhancing sinks mean in practice?
options: Protecting forests, soils and oceans that store carbon
Implementation of the Marrakesh Accords became central
They absorb more solar energy than snow-covered tundra
Urban surfaces and haze alter the local energy balance
questions.correctAnswer: Protecting forests, soils and oceans that store carbon

questions.question: How would you classify a government building-code reform?
options: Planned, public adaptation
Autonomous, private adaptation
Reactive, natural adaptation
Mitigation only

questions.question: Which strategy reduces the long-term magnitude of warming?
options: Adaptation
Mitigation
Insurance
Relocation

questions.question: What is an example of reducing emission sources?
options: It drives long-term cycling of elements among Earth spheres
Cutting fossil fuel use for electricity, heat and transport
To moderate potential damages or benefit from opportunities
Rising at oceanic ridges and descending at subduction zones
questions.correctAnswer: Cutting fossil fuel use for electricity, heat and transport

questions.question: What limitation of adaptation alone explains the need for mitigation?
options: Dark forests absorb more sunlight than snow, accelerating warming
It eases impacts but does not limit the underlying climate change
Forces that originate outside the Earth, mainly in the atmosphere
The North American Plate includes western North Atlantic seafloor
questions.correctAnswer: It eases impacts but does not limit the underlying climate change

questions.question: How do mitigation and adaptation differ in timing of benefit?
options: Ethiopia can adopt modern efficient technologies directly instead of high-emission pathways
Mitigation reduces future warming while adaptation reduces current and near-term impacts
A vent is a pipe-like opening that builds a cone; a fissure is a narrow crack that builds a plateau
Natural causes can work through all three external mechanisms while humans mainly use two
questions.correctAnswer: Mitigation reduces future warming while adaptation reduces current and near-term impacts

questions.question: Which Ethiopian practice reduces soil erosion while adapting to climate change?
options: Coal mining
Terracing
Deforestation
Overgrazing
